summary.text: 记 means “record” or “remember.” It is the simplified form of 記, whose traditional components are 言, marking the speech-and-words category, and 己, supplying a sound cue. [ref002, ref003, ref007, ref009, ref011]

formation.text: 記 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 言 contributes a meaning category, while 己 supplies the sound. This is an early dictionary analysis, not proof of the character’s original formation. 记 is the simplified form of 記. [ref008, ref017, ref030, ref037]

components.text: In 記, 言 marks the speech-and-words category. Its conventional side form 讠 appears in 记; the date and detailed path of this graphic change are not established. [ref002, ref003, ref007, ref030, ref037]
In 記, 己 is the phonetic component. Its earliest referent as a standalone character remains unsettled, a separate question from its sound role here. [ref008, ref017, ref025, ref027, ref043, ref044]

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, 記 is reconstructed as *kɯs and 己 as *kɯʔ. They share an initial and rhyme, though their endings differ. [ref033, ref043, ref045]

history.text: The received Shuowen entry analyzes 記 as 言 with 己 as its sound component and gives the gloss 疏也. A later commentary explains the gloss as distinguishing and recognizing items; another edition reads 疋也. [ref008, ref017, ref018, ref029, ref030, ref040]

記 is represented in examples labeled bronze, small-seal, and clerical. These labels show the graph in different script traditions, but do not establish exact dates, a continuous sequence, or its earliest attestation. [ref026, ref028, ref035, ref041]
记 is the simplified form of 記. The date and detailed graphic path, including the change from 言 to 讠 in this character, are not established. [ref003, ref037]

uncertainties.text: The received gloss 疏也 has a variant reading 疋也. Its relationship to later “record” and “remember” senses is unclear, as are the exact earliest attestation and the chronology of those meanings. [ref018, ref020, ref029, ref030, ref031, ref042]
The earliest referent of standalone 己 remains unsettled; its phonetic role in 記 is a separate claim in the received Shuowen analysis. [ref025, ref027, ref034, ref044]
记 is identified as simplified from 記, but the date and detailed graphic steps from 言 to 讠 are not established. [ref003, ref037]

senses.period: Eastern Han dictionary account; exact earliest use unresolved
senses.text: The received Shuowen entry gives this gloss. A later commentary and an edition variant differ in interpreting or transmitting it, so it records the dictionary’s account rather than proving the character’s earliest word sense. [ref008, ref017, ref018, ref029, ref030]

senses.period: Attested in a cited Hou Hanshu context; exact date of surviving witness unresolved
senses.text: A cited Hou Hanshu passage uses 記 for remembering. This attests the use in that context, but does not show when the sense began or how it relates to the Shuowen gloss. [ref020, ref031]

senses.period: Attested in a cited Hanshu context; exact date of surviving witness unresolved
senses.text: A cited Hanshu passage uses 記 for “record.” This attests the use in context, but does not establish a semantic transition from “remember” or from the Shuowen gloss. [ref020, ref031]

Dictionary entries include “written record” or “document” among the noun senses. Their ordering does not establish when this sense arose or its precise relation to the verbal senses. [ref021, ref022, ref030, ref042]

senses.period: Later range includes a cited Ming example
senses.text: A dictionary records a narrative genre and cites a Ming example. This documents the sense but does not establish how it developed from the verbal or documentary senses. [ref021, ref049]
Modern dictionary glosses include both recording and retaining an impression in the mind. [ref004, ref011, ref021, ref049]

limitations.text: Historical contexts attest “remember” and “record,” and later sources document noun senses, but the evidence does not establish a chronological chain among them or their connection to the received Shuowen gloss. [ref018, ref020, ref021, ref022, ref031, ref049]
The exact earliest attestation of 記 and dates of the cited textual witnesses remain unresolved. [ref020, ref026, ref031, ref035, ref041]

overview.text: 记 means “record” or “remember.” Its traditional form 記 combines 言, marking the speech-and-words category, with 己 as a sound component. [ref002, ref003, ref007, ref009, ref011]

components.text: In 記, 言 marks the speech-and-words category; in 记 it appears as the side form 讠. [ref002, ref003, ref007, ref037]
In 記, 己 supplies the sound cue; its earliest referent as a standalone character remains unsettled. [ref008, ref017, ref025, ref027]

relationships.text: The 讠 side form in 记 corresponds to 言, which the received analysis assigns a meaning-category role in traditional 記. [ref002, ref003, ref007, ref030, ref037]
The received Shuowen analysis assigns 己 the phonetic role in 記; Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstructions report compatible initial and rhyme features. [ref008, ref017, ref043, ref045]
记 is identified as the simplified form of 記. [ref003, ref037]

limitations.text: No usable glyph image is available to illustrate the character. A seal-style digital rendering was identified, but its direct image URL returned 404; the other attempted image sources could not be verified. The evidence supports the received Shuowen analysis of 記 as 言 with 己 as phonetic, but does not provide an inspectable glyph image for this selection.
